_comment: THE source for the execution traces. `node scripts/gen-traces.mjs` renders
this twice: as the ASCII blocks inside src/content/docs/internals/execution.md,
and as the JSON blob behind the call-paths page. Editing either output by hand
is how the two drift apart — which is exactly the D-11 smell the register
Hop fields: label (the code expression) · at ('file.rs:123', or ':123' to
inherit the nearest ancestor's file) · note (continuation lines, rendered
indented and not as tree children) · mark ('P1'|'P2'|'P3' for the three shared
primitives, 'warn' for a documented deviation) · ref (another trace id, drawn
as an arrow) · debt (a D-nn id) · dyn (trait name whose implementors this hop
`at` is short for display; `files` expands it to a repo path so check-anchors
can verify them. 105 hops, 99 with an anchor; before this file, zero checked.

traces.after:
`execute_parallel` (`soma-runtime/src/execution/executor.rs:1084`) is worth reading in full: it marks
`execution_order.len()`, opens a `std::thread::scope`, gives each branch a
`ctx.snapshot()` `(!)` [D-61](/soma/internals/debt/#d-61--contextsnapshot-deep-clones-the-value-store-per-branch),
then merges back only the *write set* — the entries each branch appended past
the mark.

traces.after:
`resume_with(run_id, node_id, turn, reason, answer)`
(`soma-runtime/src/agentic/mod.rs:279`) writes the answer at the *same site*, so
the next run replays into it. That is the whole resume mechanism — there is no
separate checkpoint format.

traces.title: `StreamRun`
traces.before:
Two entry points into one object. Locally, `execute_stream`
(`soma-runtime/src/execution/executor.rs:1208`) chunks the input and drives it. Remotely,
`soma-worker` holds the `StreamRun` *and its `Context`* alive in `active_streams`
between WebSocket messages and calls the same three methods itself.

children.label: Barrier  → buffer the value, stop the cascade
▸ probe_cache(…)  → tally, no per-chunk span
note: totals reported once, by finish() → NodeCacheSummary

children.label: run.flush(ctx, cache)  → materialize_buffer per barrier node
run.finish(ctx)  → NodeCacheSummary + NodeCompleted per node
note: counts as data, and "stream: N chunks, H hits, M misses" as prose

traces.after:
`FixedState` keys are **identical** to the batch path's, so a single-chunk stream
and a plain `forward` share one cache line. That invariant is what makes the
four primitives worth having.
